use: Under the Green close-range machinery material atlas
prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production game material atlas, a square image divided into EXACTLY four equally sized square material swatches, a strict 2 by 2 grid with no gutters, margins, labels or borders. High resolution meticulously hand-clustered pixel art for a damp, grim underground golf-course irrigation pump in a horror game. This is flat orthographic base-color material art for real 3D machinery, NOT a scene or a drawing of an object. Top-left: aged dark desaturated bottle-green enamel over cast iron, broad quiet intact paint areas (roughly 70 percent) interrupted by irregular chipped paint clusters, small islands of dark brown corrosion, subtle scratches and limited darker oil stains; no grooves or panel seams. Top-right: worn neutral gray bare iron/steel, restrained cool-gray and warm-gray pixel clusters, scattered shallow pits and short rubbing scratches, darker oxidized islands, mostly quiet middle-gray surface; no chrome reflections, shiny stripes, seams or rivets. Bottom-left: worn deep brick-red industrial enamel, mostly intact muted red, selectively chipped small edges and dull dark gray exposed iron islands, fine abrasion, no white highlights. Bottom-right: layered dull burnt-umber rust and blackened iron, compact flaking clusters and small exposed cool-gray islands, natural varied scale, no bright orange. Every swatch fills its exact quadrant edge to edge and is tileable on both axes. All four have the same fine pixel-cluster scale. Deliberate crisp pixel steps and clustered material marks, high-resolution pixel art, limited restrained colors per material, understated dark gritty horror tone. Flat even neutral diffuse illumination with NO baked directional shadows, NO specular highlights, no ambient glow. No photograph grain, no uniformly noisy speckles, no brush smearing, no blur, no large repeated motifs, no mechanical geometry drawn into the swatches. Real meshes supply bolts, ribs, seams, depth and dynamic lamplight. The green and red must be distinct even in dim light. The four swatches are separate textures, not one blended surface.
